tasks.task: Establish site and confirm crane hardstand readiness
tasks.scope: Set up site compound, mark exclusion zones, confirm hardstand surface bearing, verify service and utility clearances, establish communication protocol for crane operations.
hazards: Uncontrolled excavation or ground disturbance exposing underground utility (power, water, gas, telecom)
Hardstand bearing failure under crane outrigger load due to unsuitable or untested ground
Person struck by vehicle during site setup and material delivery
Trip and fall hazard from temporary site infrastructure (cables, pegs, markers)
tasks.dominant_hazard: Underground utility strike during site preparation
controls: Call Dial Before You Dig (1100) and obtain utility locates for all underground services (power, water, gas, telecom) before any ground disturbance or peg marking.
Confirm utility marks on site match ground conditions. Stop work and revalidate locates if marks are unclear or absent.
Engage engineer to assess hardstand surface bearing capacity. Obtain written certification that ground is suitable for mobile crane outrigger loads and confirm no settling or soft pockets exist.
Mark exclusion zone around crane operating area (minimum 1.5× boom radius when slewed) with high-visibility tape and portable barriers. Post signage at each entrance.
Establish communication protocol: site induction to nominate radio channel, designated spotter, and hand signals. Brief all site workers and delivery drivers before first movement.
Check all temporary site infrastructure (power cables, air hoses, communication lines) are routed clear of vehicle paths and pedestrian areas. Secure cables to prevent trip hazards.
Confirm mobile crane operator holds current C6 licence and has sight of hardstand assessment before crane arrival.
Conduct pre-mobilisation toolbox with site team on exclusion zones, communication protocol, and utility strike risk. Record attendance and sign-off.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not place crane outriggers until: engineer-certified hardstand assessment confirms ground bearing capacity and site supervisor has signed off ground conditions.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow any vehicle or personnel movement on site until: utility locates are confirmed, exclusion zones are marked, and all-workers briefed on communication protocol.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Dial Before You Dig locates are not obtained or are unclear before any ground disturbance.
🛑 STOP WORK if: ground conditions differ from hardstand assessment (soft spots, settling, water, unsuitable material encountered).
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached by unauthorised personnel or vehicles.
admin: Obtain Dial Before You Dig utility locate report and file on site.
Obtain written engineer certification of hardstand bearing capacity.
Record site induction attendance and communication protocol sign-off.
Maintain site map showing utility marks, exclusion zones, and hardstand extent.
ppe: High-visibility vest (site-wide throughout setup and crane operations)
Hard hat (when near crane or temporary infrastructure)

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.frequency: before site setup commences and at each shift start if work spans multiple days
monitoring.evidence: Dial Before You Dig report filed on site; utility marks visible and photographed; hardstand assessment document on file; induction sign-off sheet completed.

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Position and set up 25t mobile crane with safety checks
tasks.scope: Deliver crane to hardstand, position and level, confirm outrigger placement and bearing, test all safety systems, establish exclusion zone and signage for crane swing radius.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Crane tip-over due to uneven outrigger bearing or insufficient ground bearing capacity
Person struck by crane during positioning and outrigger deployment
Failure of crane safety system (brake, load limiter, hoist) undetected before operation
Crane contact with overhead power line or other utility during positioning or slew test
Person struck or crushed within crane swing radius during setup
tasks.dominant_hazard: Crane tip-over — loss of stability on hardstand
controls: Obtain engineer-certified ground bearing assessment before crane arrival; confirm hardstand capacity ≥125% of crane tare weight and maximum lifted load.
Position outriggers on level, compacted hardstand; use outrigger pads or spreader plates if ground is soft or uneven.
Check all outriggers deployed fully and locked in position; verify level using spirit level on crane chassis—do not operate if tilt >1°.
Test load limiter, hoist brake, slew brake, and emergency stop before first lift; record test results and operator sign-off.
Establish exclusion zone around full crane swing radius plus 2 m; install high-visibility barriers and signage prohibiting entry during setup and operation.
Position crane so outrigger footprint does not cross excavation edge or unsupported ground; maintain minimum 2 m setback from unsupported slope.
Brief all personnel on site about crane exclusion zone; confirm no unauthorised entry during boom positioning and slew test.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not position outriggers until: engineer-certified ground bearing assessment is sighted and hardstand condition matches engineer assumptions.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start lifting operations until: all safety system tests are recorded, documented, and signed off by crane operator and site supervisor.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: outrigger base shifts, settles, or tilts during positioning—do not re-level without engineer re-assessment.
🛑 STOP WORK if: safety system test fails (load limiter does not engage, brake does not hold, emergency stop does not activate).
🛑 STOP WORK if: overhead power line clearance cannot be confirmed or is less than 5 m.
admin: Obtain and hold on site: engineer-certified ground bearing capacity certificate before crane arrival.
Record crane position, outrigger configuration, and safety system test results on site logbook; retain for project file.
Verify crane operator holds current C6 mobile crane licence (SafeWork NSW); sighting copy before work starts.
Confirm exclusion zone signage is installed and legible before crane positioning commences.
Brief all site personnel on crane exclusion zone boundaries and no-go rules.
ppe: High-visibility vest (Day-Glo Yellow or Orange, AS/NZS 1906.4) worn by all personnel within 50 m of crane.
Hard hat (AS/NZS 1801) worn by all personnel on hardstand during crane setup.
Steel-capped boots (AS/NZS 2210) worn by crane operator and ground support personnel.

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.frequency: Before each lift commenced
monitoring.evidence: Site logbook entry, photo of level reading, operator signature

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Obtain structural engineer inspection and temporary works release
tasks.scope: Engineer inspects all permanent connections, member alignment, and prop loading. Confirms structural stability. Issues written approval for temporary prop removal and final acceptance.
hazards: Engineer inspection identifies non-conforming connection or prop loading, work must be rework or corrected
Structural engineer withholds approval pending correction or further investigation
Temporary works release is delayed, schedule impact and on-site resource delay
tasks.dominant_hazard: Engineer inspection identifies structural non-conformance — work stalled pending correction
controls: Provide engineer with current as-built drawings, prop load calculations, connection details, and inspection photos before site visit.
Brief engineer on all temporary works methods, prop types, base conditions, and load paths before inspection commences.
Stop all work on temporary works and structural alterations during engineer inspection — no adjustments or concealment of defects.
Record engineer findings in writing, naming specific non-conformance, corrective action required, and approval condition.
If non-conformance found, isolate affected area, prohibit further loading, and issue work instruction for correction before re-inspection.
Obtain written engineer approval before removing any temporary prop, releasing lateral bracing, or progressing to next structural stage.
Confirm engineer sign-off states: date, location, member or connection inspected, load condition confirmed, and release authority.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove temporary props or release lateral bracing until: structural engineer has inspected all permanent connections, verified member alignment and prop loading per design, and issued written approval naming the specific release scope and date.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: engineer inspection identifies non-conformance and withholds approval until correction is completed and re-inspected.
🛑 STOP WORK if: prop loading exceeds engineer design assumption or base condition differs from assessment.
🛑 STOP WORK if: connection, member, or alignment cannot be verified against engineer design drawings.
admin: Nominate single engineer contact with authority to issue temporary works release — name and contact on site notice.
Schedule engineer inspection at least 5 working days before planned prop removal — allow time for correction if required.
Record engineer approval in project diary and attach signed inspection report to temporary works file.
Do not permit site modifications to temporary works design or loading method without written engineer instruction.
If correction is required, obtain revised engineer approval before work resumes — do not proceed on verbal or email-only approval.

monitoring.critical_control: Verify engineer inspection report is signed and dated before proceeding — do not rely on verbal approval.
monitoring.frequency: before each temporary works release stage
monitoring.evidence: Signed engineer inspection report filed with temporary works documentation

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Obtain structural engineer inspection and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Obtain structural engineer inspection and per SWMS

tasks.task: Deliver and stage portal frame bays and loose members to site
tasks.scope: Unload and position portal frame bays, purlins, girts, and bolted connection materials in staged sequence. check for transport damage, verify member dimensions and grade stamps.
hazards: Portal frame bay or member dropped during unload, striking person or damaging member
Unstable stacking of staged members causing collapse onto person or equipment
Member transport damage undetected, leading to hidden defect in service
Person struck by mobile crane or unloader during unload and positioning sequence
tasks.dominant_hazard: Portal frame bay or member dropped during unload
controls: Obtain lift plan from structural engineer naming each bay, member weight, ground bearing condition, and exclusion zone before crane arrival.
Establish exclusion zone 1.5× longest member length around unload and staging area; barricade and post lookout to prevent unauthorised entry.
Check mobile crane operator licence (C6 minimum), load charts, and brake function before first lift; verify ground bearing capacity meets lift plan.
Brief all personnel on signal system, member identification, staging sequence, and no-go stop-work triggers before unload starts.
Unload each bay using dedicated spreader bar or approved lifting lugs only; check lugs for damage or looseness before attachment.
Position portal frame bays on level ground with minimum 0.5 m clearance between stacks; place timber packing under all contact points.
Stack loose purlins, girts, and connection materials horizontally on level ground with timber stops at each end to prevent roll-out.
check each member for transport damage (cracks, dents, bent flanges) immediately after unload; mark and segregate damaged items for engineer assessment.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not position or stage any bay or member until: structural engineer has approved lift plan in writing, ground bearing certification is on site, and exclusion zone is fully established and guarded.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to next bay until: previous bay is secured on stable base, inspected for transport damage, and confirmed free of defects or documented for assessment.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: mobile crane brake function fails, load chart limits are exceeded, or operator cannot maintain safe control.
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached by personnel or unauthorised equipment during any lift or positioning.
🛑 STOP WORK if: member shows visible crack, fracture, or structural damage that may affect its load-bearing capacity.
admin: Obtain structural engineer's lift plan before site delivery; include member weights, ground bearing, staging sequence, and engineer name.
Obtain ground bearing assessment (engineer certification) before mobile crane setup.
Verify mobile crane operator holds valid C6 licence or equivalent and has load chart for this project.
Complete delivery docket inspection against purchase order; record any transport damage immediately on docket and tell project manager.
Record member grade stamps, dimension verification, and defect assessment on stage inspection checklist; retain evidence on site.
Induct all personnel involved in unload and staging on signal system, exclusion zone rules, and stop-work triggers.
ppe: Ear protection (plugs or muff) if ambient noise exceeds 85 dB during crane operation

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during unload and positioning sequence
monitoring.evidence: Barricade intact, lookout briefed and positioned, no breach incidents recorded on site log

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Deliver and stage portal frame
responsibility.WKR: Perform Deliver and stage portal frame per SWMS

tasks.task: Prepare temporary prop bases and bearing pads
tasks.scope: Position and level temporary prop bases per engineer drawing. Install timber packing where required to achieve correct bearing and alignment. Check bearing surface stability and load capacity.
hazards: Bearing pad or timber packing shifts or fails under prop load, causing prop misalignment or collapse
Uneven bearing surface causes prop to tilt, leading to eccentric load and structural instability
Person struck by temporary prop or materials during base preparation
Improper load capacity calculation or ground unsuitability undetected before prop loading
tasks.dominant_hazard: Bearing pad failure — prop collapse under load
controls: Obtain engineer drawing showing prop location, bearing pad type, load capacity, and packing thickness before base preparation starts.

Check ground bearing surface for soft spots, debris, water pooling, or compressibility by hand and foot pressure; stop work if surface cannot support prop weight or is unsuitable per engineer assessment.
Position bearing pad or timber packing on hard, level ground per engineer drawing; use shim packs (timber or steel) to achieve level plane within 10 mm across bearing area.
Verify bearing surface is clean, free from loose material, mud, and standing water; damp-wipe if required to confirm surface integrity.
Check prop base sits flush on bearing pad with no rocking, gaps, or tilting; use spirit level on two axes to confirm alignment within 5 mm.
Do not load prop until bearing base is signed off by structural engineer or nominated delegate; hold point must confirm load capacity calculation matches ground condition.
Monitor bearing pad settlement and alignment daily during prop loading; record any visible movement, tilting, or water ingress and report to engineer immediately.
Remove or replace water-logged, damaged, crushed, or non-compliant bearing pads or packing immediately; do not add load until corrective action is confirmed in writing by engineer.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not place or load prop until: engineer or nominated structural delegate has checked bearing surface, confirmed load capacity calculation, and signed off bearing pad installation per engineer drawing.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to next stage until: ground bearing assessment (if crane or heavy load method) has been certified by engineer and documented on site.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: bearing surface is soft, water-logged, compressible, or does not match engineer assessment criteria.
🛑 STOP WORK if: bearing pad or timber packing shifts, tilts, settles, or shows visible misalignment during or after prop loading.
🛑 STOP WORK if: prop or bearing base rocks, moves, or cannot be levelled to within 5 mm across bearing plane.
admin: Brief all workers on engineer drawing location, bearing pad requirements, and no-load hold point before work starts.
Record engineer sign-off of bearing pad installation, load capacity approval, and any ground condition variations in site diary.
Keep engineer drawing and ground bearing assessment on site and accessible to all workers during prop installation and loading.
Report any bearing pad movement, settlement, water damage, or structural concern to site supervisor and engineer within same shift.

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: Before prop placement; daily during prop loading; after rainfall or ground disturbance.
monitoring.evidence: Site diary entry confirming bearing pad check and level; engineer sign-off on bearing pad installation; photographic record of bearing surface and pad placement.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Prepare temporary prop bases and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Prepare temporary prop bases and per SWMS

tasks.task: Lift and position portal frame bays with crane and temporary props
tasks.scope: Crane-lift each bay into position per lift plan. Fit temporary props to plumb and stabilise. Release crane hook only after props confirmed loaded and bay movement locked. Repeat for all 8 bays.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Crane load instability or hook failure during lift, bay or member drops onto person or adjacent structure
Temporary prop fails to catch bay load or is not loaded during lift, bay collapses
Bay or member swings or rotates uncontrolled during positioning, striking person or adjacent work
Bay movement continues after props engaged, prop load exceeds design or bearing fails
Slinger or banksman struck by swinging load or within swing radius
Communication failure between crane operator and ground spotter, leading to uncontrolled movement
tasks.dominant_hazard: Portal frame bay drops during lift — prop failure or hook release before stabilisation
controls: Obtain lift plan signed by engineer before crane arrives on site — plan must confirm bay mass, rigging method, prop type, prop placement, bearing capacity, and hook release hold point.
Confirm mobile crane has current inspection certificate and operator holds valid C6 licence before first lift commences.
check all temporary props (type, model, height, base condition) against lift plan — confirm bearing area is level, solid, and capable of taking prop load.
Brief slinger, banksman, and crane operator before each bay lift — confirm communication method (radio or hand signals), no-go zones, and hold point condition.
Position banksman in clear line of sight to crane operator and bay during lift — banksman confirms bay is level, props are taking load, and bay movement has stopped before signalling hook release.
Rig bay only when props are installed, plumb, and positioned to receive load — never lift without prop base confirmed level and load-bearing surface clear of debris.
Release crane hook only after banksman confirms bay is stable on props, vertical, and not moving — do not remove hook until props have full load and bay cannot fall.
Lock bay to props or fix props to prevent bay or prop movement — use temporary welds, bolts, or bracing per lift plan before crane hook is released.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not release crane hook until: banksman confirms bay is level on props, props are fully loaded, and bay is locked to prevent movement.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start any bay lift until: lift plan is signed by engineer, all props are installed and plumb, prop bearing area is level and clear, and banksman and operator have confirmed communication.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: bay swings uncontrolled, rotates, or does not stabilise on props within 30 seconds of landing.
🛑 STOP WORK if: props shift, settle, or show signs of failure during or after load is applied.
🛑 STOP WORK if: ground conditions under prop bases differ from lift plan assessment or bearing fails.
admin: Provide copy of lift plan at site before crane mobilisation — keep on-site during all lifting work.
Record prop installation, plumb, and load confirmation on site sign-off sheet before each bay is lifted.
Brief all on-site personnel (not involved in lift) on exclusion zone before first bay lift — confirm no unauthorised entry during any lift.
check prop bearing area and bay seating daily before work starts — record findings in site book.

monitoring.critical_control: Banksman confirms bay is level, stable on props, and locked before signalling hook release.
monitoring.frequency: before each bay hook release — continuous visual confirmation during landing and load transfer
monitoring.evidence: Banksman hand signal (confirmed receipt by operator) and site sign-off sheet recording bay number, time, props engaged, and release authorised

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Lift and position portal frame
responsibility.WKR: Perform Lift and position portal frame per SWMS

tasks.task: Install purlins and secondary bracing members
tasks.scope: Crane-lift and position purlins and lateral bracing per engineer drawing. Fit and torque bolted connections. Confirm alignment and member spacing.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Purlin or bracing member dropped during crane lift, striking person or damaging bay structure
Member bolted connection failure under load due to incorrect torque or misalignment
Purlin misalignment or spacing incorrect, structural instability or deflection
Worker falls from height while accessing purlin installation points
Crane hook or sling failure during secondary member lift
tasks.dominant_hazard: Purlin or bracing member dropped during lift
controls: Obtain engineer-approved lift plan naming member weight, rigging method, exclusion zone radius, and ground bearing capacity before crane arrives on site.
Confirm mobile crane operator holds current C6 licence and check crane load chart against member weight and lift geometry.
Establish exclusion zone 1.5× member length radius around lift area. Barricade with chain and signage. Prohibit all personnel entry during lift.
check all slings, shackles, and rigging hardware for damage, wear, or deformation. Record serial and test date. Do not use if expired.
Position banksman within clear sight of crane operator and load. Use two-way radio. Brief banksman on hand signals before lift starts.
Perform trial lift to 1 m height. Hold for 10 seconds. Check sling angle, load stability, and hook alignment. Lower and reposition if movement detected.
Communicate 'load secure' signal from tag-on worker before crane hoists to working height.
During lift, maintain continuous radio contact. Stop immediately if sling twists, load swings, or crane load indicator exceeds 85% capacity.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start lift until: engineer-approved lift plan is signed by site supervisor and ground bearing assessment is certified by engineer.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not tension bolted connections until: all members are plumb, aligned, and positioned to engineer tolerances, confirmed in writing by site supervisor or structural consultant.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached by any personnel, sling or rigging hardware shows damage or deformation, or load indicator exceeds 85% of crane capacity.
🛑 STOP WORK if: member alignment or spacing deviates from engineer drawing by more than stated tolerance, or bolted connection torque cannot be achieved within specification.
admin: Brief all workers on lift plan, exclusion zone, and radio protocol before work starts.
Record lift date, member ID, rigging method, and trial lift outcome in site diary.
Record bolted connection details: bolt ID, torque wrench serial, value applied, worker initials, date.
Record final member alignment and spacing against engineer drawing on site inspection sheet.
tell structural consultant of any deviation from engineer drawing for written approval before proceeding to next bay.
ppe: High-visibility vest (Class D) — mandatory in exclusion zone and near active lift.
Hard hat — mandatory always on site.
steel-capped footwear— mandatory for ground-level rigging and positioning work.
Harness and lanyard (rated to 15 kN) — mandatory when accessing purlin installation points on frame perimeter or > 2 m height.

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone maintained and patrolled continuously during lift. Radio communication clear between crane operator and tag-on worker.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during lift. Before each member lift commences.
monitoring.evidence: Radio check-in log. Exclusion zone barricade intact. Trial lift height and hold time recorded. Bolt torque worksheet completed per connection.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install purlins and secondary bracing
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install purlins and secondary bracing per SWMS

tasks.task: Confirm structural engineer approval and lift plan before erection
tasks.scope: Review and sign-off lift plan, bracing sequence, temporary prop locations, bearing details, and permanent connection schedule. Obtain written approval before first lift commences.
hazards: Lift plan does not reflect actual site condition, prop placement, or bearing capacity
Bracing sequence or temporary prop schedule is incomplete or unworkable on site
Structural engineer approval is withheld or conditional, delaying or halting work
tasks.dominant_hazard: Lift plan inadequacy — props unable to stabilise bay or bracing sequence incomplete
controls: Obtain written lift plan from structural engineer before first lift commences — plan must include prop locations, bearing details, bracing sequence, and load path.
Check lift plan against actual site conditions — confirm prop base locations match design, bearing surfaces are level and clean, and temporary support positions are accessible.
Verify bracing sequence with engineer — confirm first brace installed before load application, sequence order marked on plan, and no unauthorised changes to prop placement.
Confirm ground bearing assessment — check engineer certification of crane pad or prop base bearing capacity before mobile crane setup or propping commences.
Review permanent connection schedule with engineer — confirm final connection procedure, temporary prop removal sequence, and hold points before props are released.
Mark hold point locations on site plan — delineate temporary prop bases with tape, paint temporary prop locations with high-visibility marking.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start any lift or install props until: structural engineer has reviewed and signed lift plan, bracing sequence, bearing details, and permanent connection schedule.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not release temporary props until: permanent connections are certified complete and engineer has inspected and approved connection integrity.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: lift plan is unsigned, incomplete, or conditions cannot be met on site.
🛑 STOP WORK if: prop base shifts, subsides, or differs from engineer detail during erection.
🛑 STOP WORK if: bracing sequence is altered, skipped, or unauthorised prop movement or release occurs.
admin: Issue written lift plan approval signed by structural engineer before work start.
Record lift plan sign-off date, time, and site conditions in project logbook.
Keep signed lift plan on site throughout erection — accessible to all trades involved.
Brief all workers and supervisors on bracing sequence and prop locations before erection starts.

monitoring.critical_control: Verify engineer-signed lift plan present and site conditions match plan before first prop installed.
monitoring.frequency: Before erection commences and daily during erection
monitoring.evidence: Signed lift plan document, site condition photographs, logbook entry confirming approval date and conditions.

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

tasks.task: Install permanent bolted connections per engineer schedule
tasks.scope: Fit and torque all bolted connections on portal frame primary members and girt connections before any prop release. Verify connection tightness and alignment. Document completion for engineer sign-off.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Bolted connection torque procedure not followed, connection left under-torqued or over-stressed
Bolt thread stripping or fastener failure during tightening or service load
Misalignment of members prevents connection seating or bolt insertion
Worker falls from height while accessing elevated connection points
Spanner or tool dropped from height strikes person below
tasks.dominant_hazard: Connection under-torqued — structural failure under load
controls: Obtain engineer-issued torque schedule and bolt specification document before any fastener is installed.
Check all bolts and fasteners for damage, corrosion, or thread defects before insertion — reject any non-compliant fasteners.
Align portal frame primary members and girt connections to engineer drawing tolerance before bolt insertion commences.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not torque bolts until: member alignment verified and documented by site supervisor.
Tighten all bolts in sequence per engineer schedule using calibrated torque wrench only — no impact tools.
Verify torque wrench calibration certificate dated within 12 months — re-calibrate if expired.
Apply torque in three passes: snug, 50% target, 100% target — record each pass on connection log.
Check final bolt tightness 24 hours after installation using calibrated torque wrench — retorque any slack connections.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not torque bolts until: member alignment verified and documented by site supervisor.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not release any temporary props until: all bolted connections torqued per schedule and final tightness verified by engineer or delegate.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: torque wrench is uncalibrated, bolt specification does not match engineer schedule, or member misalignment exceeds ±5mm.
🛑 STOP WORK if: thread stripping, fastener deformation, or bolt failure occurs during tightening.
🛑 STOP WORK if: dropped-object net is absent, damaged, or exclusion zone below connection work is breached.
admin: Maintain connection installation log recording: bolt location, size, grade, torque value applied, date, time, worker name, and verification sign-off.
Brief all workers on engineer torque schedule and bolt specification before work starts.
Provide engineer torque schedule and bolt specification document on point of use.
tell engineer or delegate when all connections are torqued and ready for final sign-off — do not release props until approval received.
Confirm calibration certificate for torque wrench is current and displayed on site.
ppe: Fall arrest harness and lanyard (AS/NZS 1891.1) — mandatory for all work >2m above ground level

monitoring.critical_control: Verify torque wrench calibration certificate is current and within 12-month interval.
monitoring.who: Site supervisor before each work day.
monitoring.frequency: Daily, before first bolt is tightened.
monitoring.evidence: Calibration certificate sighted and dated on site logbook.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install permanent bolted connections per
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install permanent bolted connections per per SWMS

tasks.task: Remove temporary props under engineer written approval only
tasks.scope: After engineer sign-off, carefully remove temporary props in reverse erection sequence. Check member plumb and connection security as each prop is released. Document removal.
hazards: Prop removed in incorrect sequence, causing bay movement or loss of stability before permanent connection load transfer
Member plumb or alignment lost during prop removal, structural instability or misalignment undetected
Connection failure occurs on prop removal, bay collapse or unexpected movement
Worker struck by prop or member during removal or by falling debris
Prop removal without engineer written approval, structural stability unknown
tasks.dominant_hazard: Bay movement or collapse during prop removal — incorrect sequence or connection failure
controls: Obtain engineer written sign-off on permanent connection load transfer before any prop removal commences.
Remove props in strict reverse erection sequence as documented on engineer temporary works plan.
Check plumb and alignment of member immediately after each prop release using levels and datum points.
Verify connection bolts or welds remain secure and fully engaged after each prop removal.
Stop all removal work immediately if member movement, deflection, or misalignment is detected.
Barricade removal area to exclude unauthorised personnel and prevent struck-by incidents.
Document each prop removed, time, worker name, and plumb confirmation in removal log before next prop removal.
Position workers clear of prop release path and falling member zones during removal.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove any prop until: Engineer written approval and permanent connection load transfer documentation is received and signed.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove next prop until: Previous prop removal is documented, plumb is confirmed, and connection security is verified.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Member plumb or alignment cannot be confirmed after prop removal.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Connection bolts are loose, partially engaged, or welds show cracks or separation.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Unexpected movement, deflection, or noise occurs during or immediately after prop removal.
admin: Supervisor to brief all workers on reverse erection sequence before work starts.
Retain engineer temporary works plan on site and accessible to removal crew.
Maintain removal log with date, time, prop ID, plumb confirmation, and worker sign-off.
tell structural engineer immediately if any removal condition differs from engineer plan.

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: After each prop removed
monitoring.evidence: Removal log signed by worker and supervisor with plumb confirmation and connection status recorded.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove temporary props under engineer
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove temporary props under engineer per SWMS

tasks.task: Final inspection and handover to principal contractor
tasks.scope: Confirm all structural work complete to design and engineer approval. Remove all exclusion signage. Provide as-built documentation and engineer sign-off to principal contractor.
hazards: As-built documentation incomplete or does not match engineer sign-off and design
Structural defect or non-conformance not identified during final inspection
Exclusion signage not fully removed, creating confusion on site
tasks.dominant_hazard: Structural defect unidentified at handover — latent failure risk in service
controls: Obtain engineer final sign-off checklist before starting inspection—confirm all design requirements, material certificates, and tolerances are listed.

Monitor bearing pad settlement and alignment daily during prop loading; record any visible movement, tilting, or water ingress and report to engineer immediately.
Remove or replace water-logged, damaged, crushed, or non-compliant bearing pads or packing immediately; do not add load until corrective action is confirmed in writing by engineer.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not place or load prop until: engineer or nominated structural delegate has checked bearing surface, confirmed load capacity calculation, and signed off bearing pad installation per engineer drawing.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to next stage until: ground bearing assessment (if crane or heavy load method) has been certified by engineer and documented on site.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: bearing surface is soft, water-logged, compressible, or does not match engineer assessment criteria.
🛑 STOP WORK if: bearing pad or timber packing shifts, tilts, settles, or shows visible misalignment during or after prop loading.
🛑 STOP WORK if: prop or bearing base rocks, moves, or cannot be levelled to within 5 mm across bearing plane.
admin: Brief all workers on engineer drawing location, bearing pad requirements, and no-load hold point before work starts.
Record engineer sign-off of bearing pad installation, load capacity approval, and any ground condition variations in site diary.
Keep engineer drawing and ground bearing assessment on site and accessible to all workers during prop installation and loading.
Report any bearing pad movement, settlement, water damage, or structural concern to site supervisor and engineer within same shift.

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: Before prop placement; daily during prop loading; after rainfall or ground disturbance.
monitoring.evidence: Site diary entry confirming bearing pad check and level; engineer sign-off on bearing pad installation; photographic record of bearing surface and pad placement.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Prepare temporary prop bases and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Prepare temporary prop bases and per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Lift and position portal frame bays with crane and temporary props
task_blocks_raw.scope: Crane-lift each bay into position per lift plan. Fit temporary props to plumb and stabilise. Release crane hook only after props confirmed loaded and bay movement locked. Repeat for all 8 bays.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Crane load instability or hook failure during lift, bay or member drops onto person or adjacent structure
Temporary prop fails to catch bay load or is not loaded during lift, bay collapses
Bay or member swings or rotates uncontrolled during positioning, striking person or adjacent work
Bay movement continues after props engaged, prop load exceeds design or bearing fails
Slinger or banksman struck by swinging load or within swing radius
Communication failure between crane operator and ground spotter, leading to uncontrolled movement
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Portal frame bay drops during lift — prop failure or hook release before stabilisation
controls: Obtain lift plan signed by engineer before crane arrives on site — plan must confirm bay mass, rigging method, prop type, prop placement, bearing capacity, and hook release hold point.
Confirm mobile crane has current inspection certificate and operator holds valid C6 licence before first lift commences.
check all temporary props (type, model, height, base condition) against lift plan — confirm bearing area is level, solid, and capable of taking prop load.
Brief slinger, banksman, and crane operator before each bay lift — confirm communication method (radio or hand signals), no-go zones, and hold point condition.
Position banksman in clear line of sight to crane operator and bay during lift — banksman confirms bay is level, props are taking load, and bay movement has stopped before signalling hook release.
Rig bay only when props are installed, plumb, and positioned to receive load — never lift without prop base confirmed level and load-bearing surface clear of debris.
Release crane hook only after banksman confirms bay is stable on props, vertical, and not moving — do not remove hook until props have full load and bay cannot fall.
Lock bay to props or fix props to prevent bay or prop movement — use temporary welds, bolts, or bracing per lift plan before crane hook is released.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not release crane hook until: banksman confirms bay is level on props, props are fully loaded, and bay is locked to prevent movement.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start any bay lift until: lift plan is signed by engineer, all props are installed and plumb, prop bearing area is level and clear, and banksman and operator have confirmed communication.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: bay swings uncontrolled, rotates, or does not stabilise on props within 30 seconds of landing.
🛑 STOP WORK if: props shift, settle, or show signs of failure during or after load is applied.
🛑 STOP WORK if: ground conditions under prop bases differ from lift plan assessment or bearing fails.
admin: Provide copy of lift plan at site before crane mobilisation — keep on-site during all lifting work.
Record prop installation, plumb, and load confirmation on site sign-off sheet before each bay is lifted.
Brief all on-site personnel (not involved in lift) on exclusion zone before first bay lift — confirm no unauthorised entry during any lift.
check prop bearing area and bay seating daily before work starts — record findings in site book.

monitoring.critical_control: Banksman confirms bay is level, stable on props, and locked before signalling hook release.
monitoring.frequency: before each bay hook release — continuous visual confirmation during landing and load transfer
monitoring.evidence: Banksman hand signal (confirmed receipt by operator) and site sign-off sheet recording bay number, time, props engaged, and release authorised

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Lift and position portal frame
responsibility.WKR: Perform Lift and position portal frame per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Install permanent bolted connections per engineer schedule
task_blocks_raw.scope: Fit and torque all bolted connections on portal frame primary members and girt connections before any prop release. Verify connection tightness and alignment. Document completion for engineer sign-off.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Bolted connection torque procedure not followed, connection left under-torqued or over-stressed
Bolt thread stripping or fastener failure during tightening or service load
Misalignment of members prevents connection seating or bolt insertion
Worker falls from height while accessing elevated connection points
Spanner or tool dropped from height strikes person below
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Connection under-torqued — structural failure under load
controls: Obtain engineer-issued torque schedule and bolt specification document before any fastener is installed.
Check all bolts and fasteners for damage, corrosion, or thread defects before insertion — reject any non-compliant fasteners.
Align portal frame primary members and girt connections to engineer drawing tolerance before bolt insertion commences.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not torque bolts until: member alignment verified and documented by site supervisor.
Tighten all bolts in sequence per engineer schedule using calibrated torque wrench only — no impact tools.
Verify torque wrench calibration certificate dated within 12 months — re-calibrate if expired.
Apply torque in three passes: snug, 50% target, 100% target — record each pass on connection log.
Check final bolt tightness 24 hours after installation using calibrated torque wrench — retorque any slack connections.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not torque bolts until: member alignment verified and documented by site supervisor.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not release any temporary props until: all bolted connections torqued per schedule and final tightness verified by engineer or delegate.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: torque wrench is uncalibrated, bolt specification does not match engineer schedule, or member misalignment exceeds ±5mm.
🛑 STOP WORK if: thread stripping, fastener deformation, or bolt failure occurs during tightening.
🛑 STOP WORK if: dropped-object net is absent, damaged, or exclusion zone below connection work is breached.
admin: Maintain connection installation log recording: bolt location, size, grade, torque value applied, date, time, worker name, and verification sign-off.
Brief all workers on engineer torque schedule and bolt specification before work starts.
Provide engineer torque schedule and bolt specification document on point of use.
tell engineer or delegate when all connections are torqued and ready for final sign-off — do not release props until approval received.
Confirm calibration certificate for torque wrench is current and displayed on site.
ppe: Fall arrest harness and lanyard (AS/NZS 1891.1) — mandatory for all work >2m above ground level

monitoring.critical_control: Verify torque wrench calibration certificate is current and within 12-month interval.
monitoring.who: Site supervisor before each work day.
monitoring.frequency: Daily, before first bolt is tightened.
monitoring.evidence: Calibration certificate sighted and dated on site logbook.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install permanent bolted connections per
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install permanent bolted connections per per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Install purlins and secondary bracing members
task_blocks_raw.scope: Crane-lift and position purlins and lateral bracing per engineer drawing. Fit and torque bolted connections. Confirm alignment and member spacing.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Purlin or bracing member dropped during crane lift, striking person or damaging bay structure
Member bolted connection failure under load due to incorrect torque or misalignment
Purlin misalignment or spacing incorrect, structural instability or deflection
Worker falls from height while accessing purlin installation points
Crane hook or sling failure during secondary member lift
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Purlin or bracing member dropped during lift
controls: Obtain engineer-approved lift plan naming member weight, rigging method, exclusion zone radius, and ground bearing capacity before crane arrives on site.
Confirm mobile crane operator holds current C6 licence and check crane load chart against member weight and lift geometry.
Establish exclusion zone 1.5× member length radius around lift area. Barricade with chain and signage. Prohibit all personnel entry during lift.
check all slings, shackles, and rigging hardware for damage, wear, or deformation. Record serial and test date. Do not use if expired.
Position banksman within clear sight of crane operator and load. Use two-way radio. Brief banksman on hand signals before lift starts.
Perform trial lift to 1 m height. Hold for 10 seconds. Check sling angle, load stability, and hook alignment. Lower and reposition if movement detected.
Communicate 'load secure' signal from tag-on worker before crane hoists to working height.
During lift, maintain continuous radio contact. Stop immediately if sling twists, load swings, or crane load indicator exceeds 85% capacity.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start lift until: engineer-approved lift plan is signed by site supervisor and ground bearing assessment is certified by engineer.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not tension bolted connections until: all members are plumb, aligned, and positioned to engineer tolerances, confirmed in writing by site supervisor or structural consultant.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached by any personnel, sling or rigging hardware shows damage or deformation, or load indicator exceeds 85% of crane capacity.
🛑 STOP WORK if: member alignment or spacing deviates from engineer drawing by more than stated tolerance, or bolted connection torque cannot be achieved within specification.
admin: Brief all workers on lift plan, exclusion zone, and radio protocol before work starts.
Record lift date, member ID, rigging method, and trial lift outcome in site diary.
Record bolted connection details: bolt ID, torque wrench serial, value applied, worker initials, date.
Record final member alignment and spacing against engineer drawing on site inspection sheet.
tell structural consultant of any deviation from engineer drawing for written approval before proceeding to next bay.
ppe: High-visibility vest (Class D) — mandatory in exclusion zone and near active lift.
Hard hat — mandatory always on site.
steel-capped footwear— mandatory for ground-level rigging and positioning work.
Harness and lanyard (rated to 15 kN) — mandatory when accessing purlin installation points on frame perimeter or > 2 m height.

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone maintained and patrolled continuously during lift. Radio communication clear between crane operator and tag-on worker.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during lift. Before each member lift commences.
monitoring.evidence: Radio check-in log. Exclusion zone barricade intact. Trial lift height and hold time recorded. Bolt torque worksheet completed per connection.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install purlins and secondary bracing
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install purlins and secondary bracing per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Obtain structural engineer inspection and temporary works release
task_blocks_raw.scope: Engineer inspects all permanent connections, member alignment, and prop loading. Confirms structural stability. Issues written approval for temporary prop removal and final acceptance.
hazards: Engineer inspection identifies non-conforming connection or prop loading, work must be rework or corrected
Structural engineer withholds approval pending correction or further investigation
Temporary works release is delayed, schedule impact and on-site resource delay
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Engineer inspection identifies structural non-conformance — work stalled pending correction
controls: Provide engineer with current as-built drawings, prop load calculations, connection details, and inspection photos before site visit.
Brief engineer on all temporary works methods, prop types, base conditions, and load paths before inspection commences.
Stop all work on temporary works and structural alterations during engineer inspection — no adjustments or concealment of defects.
Record engineer findings in writing, naming specific non-conformance, corrective action required, and approval condition.
If non-conformance found, isolate affected area, prohibit further loading, and issue work instruction for correction before re-inspection.
Obtain written engineer approval before removing any temporary prop, releasing lateral bracing, or progressing to next structural stage.
Confirm engineer sign-off states: date, location, member or connection inspected, load condition confirmed, and release authority.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove temporary props or release lateral bracing until: structural engineer has inspected all permanent connections, verified member alignment and prop loading per design, and issued written approval naming the specific release scope and date.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: engineer inspection identifies non-conformance and withholds approval until correction is completed and re-inspected.
🛑 STOP WORK if: prop loading exceeds engineer design assumption or base condition differs from assessment.
🛑 STOP WORK if: connection, member, or alignment cannot be verified against engineer design drawings.
admin: Nominate single engineer contact with authority to issue temporary works release — name and contact on site notice.
Schedule engineer inspection at least 5 working days before planned prop removal — allow time for correction if required.
Record engineer approval in project diary and attach signed inspection report to temporary works file.
Do not permit site modifications to temporary works design or loading method without written engineer instruction.
If correction is required, obtain revised engineer approval before work resumes — do not proceed on verbal or email-only approval.

monitoring.critical_control: Verify engineer inspection report is signed and dated before proceeding — do not rely on verbal approval.
monitoring.frequency: before each temporary works release stage
monitoring.evidence: Signed engineer inspection report filed with temporary works documentation

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Obtain structural engineer inspection and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Obtain structural engineer inspection and per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Remove temporary props under engineer written approval only
task_blocks_raw.scope: After engineer sign-off, carefully remove temporary props in reverse erection sequence. Check member plumb and connection security as each prop is released. Document removal.
hazards: Prop removed in incorrect sequence, causing bay movement or loss of stability before permanent connection load transfer
Member plumb or alignment lost during prop removal, structural instability or misalignment undetected
Connection failure occurs on prop removal, bay collapse or unexpected movement
Worker struck by prop or member during removal or by falling debris
Prop removal without engineer written approval, structural stability unknown
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Bay movement or collapse during prop removal — incorrect sequence or connection failure
controls: Obtain engineer written sign-off on permanent connection load transfer before any prop removal commences.
Remove props in strict reverse erection sequence as documented on engineer temporary works plan.
Check plumb and alignment of member immediately after each prop release using levels and datum points.
Verify connection bolts or welds remain secure and fully engaged after each prop removal.
Stop all removal work immediately if member movement, deflection, or misalignment is detected.
Barricade removal area to exclude unauthorised personnel and prevent struck-by incidents.
Document each prop removed, time, worker name, and plumb confirmation in removal log before next prop removal.
Position workers clear of prop release path and falling member zones during removal.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove any prop until: Engineer written approval and permanent connection load transfer documentation is received and signed.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove next prop until: Previous prop removal is documented, plumb is confirmed, and connection security is verified.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Member plumb or alignment cannot be confirmed after prop removal.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Connection bolts are loose, partially engaged, or welds show cracks or separation.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Unexpected movement, deflection, or noise occurs during or immediately after prop removal.
admin: Supervisor to brief all workers on reverse erection sequence before work starts.
Retain engineer temporary works plan on site and accessible to removal crew.
Maintain removal log with date, time, prop ID, plumb confirmation, and worker sign-off.
tell structural engineer immediately if any removal condition differs from engineer plan.

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: After each prop removed
monitoring.evidence: Removal log signed by worker and supervisor with plumb confirmation and connection status recorded.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove temporary props under engineer
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove temporary props under engineer per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Remove crane and demobilise site plant
task_blocks_raw.scope: Safely stand crane down from hardstand. Remove all temporary plant, access equipment, and hardstand staging materials. Clear site of construction debris.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Crane movement or stand-down uncontrolled, crane tip-over or contact with structure or utility
Person struck by crane or temporary plant during demobilisation
Temporary hardstand or staging materials not properly dismantled, trip or fall hazard
Site debris left uncleared, creating trip or fall hazard or environmental risk
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Crane tip-over during stand-down or uncontrolled movement
controls: Obtain crane operator's final position assessment — confirm crane is stable, counterweight and boom secured, no load on hook before stand-down begins.
Verify hardstand bearing capacity and condition before crane stand-down — check for settlement, soft spots, or water pooling; if failed, stop work and reassess.
Establish exclusion zone minimum 1.5 × boom length around crane — barricade with tape and signage; no personnel within zone during any crane movement.
Brief all personnel on stand-down sequence and exclusion zone before work starts — confirm understanding and assign spotters.
Appoint competent spotter with direct line of sight to operator — continuous radio communication during all crane movements; spotter must confirm 'all clear' before each movement.
Dismantle temporary hardstand staging in reverse sequence of erection — remove props, bracing, and base materials only after engineer or site supervisor confirms no load transfer risk.
Segregate all removed temporary plant and debris into designated skip bins or storage areas — do not leave materials on walkways, access routes, or near building edges.
Remove all site debris daily as work progresses — final clear-up must remove all scraps, offcuts, broken materials, and dust before handover.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start crane stand-down until: crane operator and site supervisor jointly confirm hardstand bearing, counterweight security, boom securing, and exclusion zone establishment.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove temporary hardstand materials until: engineer or site supervisor has signed off that no load transfer or structural dependency exists.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: crane shows any movement, settlement, or tilt during stand-down; operator reports instability or hydraulic anomaly.
🛑 STOP WORK if: personnel enter or remain in exclusion zone; spotter loses line of sight or radio communication fails.
🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 40 km/h, rain restricts visibility, or weather deteriorates unexpectedly.
admin: Confirm crane operator holds current C6 (mobile) or C2 (tower) licence — copy on file before stand-down.
Record hardstand final condition assessment — date, name, sign-off by site supervisor.
Record exclusion zone confirmation and personnel briefing attendance — sign-in sheet.
Document final debris removal and site clear — photographic evidence or sign-off by site supervisor.
tell site manager and client of demobilisation completion before crane leaves site.
ppe: Ear protection if noise exceeds 85 dB during crane or plant movement

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.who: Crane operator, appointed spotter, site supervisor
monitoring.frequency: Before each crane movement; continuous during stand-down; final check before crane leaves site
monitoring.evidence: Radio log or hand signals recorded; exclusion zone remains barricaded and unbreached; no personnel within zone during movement; hardstand engineer sign-off on file; debris removal photographic evidence.

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

task_blocks_raw.task: Final inspection and handover to principal contractor
task_blocks_raw.scope: Confirm all structural work complete to design and engineer approval. Remove all exclusion signage. Provide as-built documentation and engineer sign-off to principal contractor.
hazards: As-built documentation incomplete or does not match engineer sign-off and design
Structural defect or non-conformance not identified during final inspection
Exclusion signage not fully removed, creating confusion on site
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Structural defect unidentified at handover — latent failure risk in service
controls: Obtain engineer final sign-off checklist before starting inspection—confirm all design requirements, material certificates, and tolerances are listed.
Conduct physical inspection against engineer checklist: check all structural connections, welds (if applicable), column alignment, beam deflection, and concrete curing—record findings on site.
Compare as-built drawings with design drawings—identify and document any deviations, cuts, or amendments made during construction.
Collect all material test certificates, NDT reports, welding records, and concrete strength results—verify they match installed elements.
Hold point: do not remove exclusion signage until engineer confirms all structural work meets design and issues final sign-off certificate.
Remove all exclusion tape, barrier signs, and restricted-area notices—photograph removal and confirm no signage remains.
Prepare as-built documentation package: bundle final drawings, engineer sign-off, test certificates, and inspection record—deliver to principal contractor with written receipt.
Obtain principal contractor sign-off acknowledging receipt of as-built documentation and acceptance of structural work.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove exclusion signage until: engineer completes final inspection, confirms all structural work conforms to design, and issues signed-off certificate on site
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: physical inspection reveals structural defect, non-conformance, or deviation not recorded in engineer amendment log
🛑 STOP WORK if: material test certificates, NDT reports, or welding records cannot be located or do not match installed elements
🛑 STOP WORK if: as-built drawings cannot be completed or contain irreconcilable differences from design
admin: Brief principal contractor on final inspection scope and timeline before work starts.
Photograph all structural elements and completed work before handover for as-built record.
Record inspection results, defects (if any), and remedial actions in site logbook.
Confirm exclusion signage removal with site supervisor—check no signage remains visible.
Retain copy of engineer final sign-off certificate and as-built documentation on file for 10 years.

monitoring.critical_control: Engineer sign-off certificate physically present and signed before any signage removal.
monitoring.who: Structural engineer / Site supervisor / Principal contractor representative
monitoring.frequency: Before final handover
monitoring.evidence: Signed engineer final sign-off certificate, completed inspection checklist, as-built documentation package receipt, photographic record of exclusion signage removal

responsibility.SUP: Supervise dismantling and demobilisation, verify controls, manage site access
responsibility.WKR: Dismantle and clear per SWMS, report hazards, obey spotter directions
